title: fix(update): recognize custom npm prefix installations
body:
Fixes #146038

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

This branch is in the upstream repository and is available for maintainer edits.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users updating an npm installation under a custom prefix such as `~/.npm-global` receive an unknown-package-manager outcome when npm's global-root probe differs from the running installation. The prefix contains an OpenClaw launcher but normally no npm executable, so the existing fallback discarded valid installation evidence.

Reported by a Discord user (Rex Horizon), support thread "As usual update fails" (#146038). The Linux installer and Node installation docs recommend this prefix layout.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared installed-owner resolver now checks npm's configured global prefix using the Node running OpenClaw, leaving npm itself responsible for npmrc precedence and expansion. It also recognizes a global OpenClaw launcher resolving into the corresponding npm package tree when command probes do not match. Windows custom prefixes use the same layout owner. Existing pnpm and Bun detection stays intact, and the selected npm update target remains the running package prefix.

Update status now uses this resolver instead of its separate lockless-package heuristic. Unknown-owner guidance includes the inspected package root, probe results, inferred prefix, and launcher path. Repair and rollback already retain the selected package transaction; Doctor delegates package updates to the same update command.

## User Impact

Updates on custom npm prefix installs (nvm + `~/.npm-global`) no longer refuse with "package manager owner is unknown" solely because the prefix has no npm executable and the global-root probe differs. Status and update admission agree about installation ownership. Unknown layouts remain unchanged and provide actionable inspection details.

## Evidence

- Installed dependencies with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline`.
- Focused proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-runner.test.ts src/infra/update-global-lifecycle.test.ts src/infra/update-global.test.ts src/infra/update-global.bun-owner.test.ts src/infra/update-global.pnpm11-discovery.test.ts src/infra/update-check-status.test.ts src/infra/update-check.test.ts src/infra/update-check-install-kind.test.ts src/infra/detect-package-manager.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/shared.command-runner.test.ts` — 335 tests passed across ten files.
- Pre-fix tests: Linux/macOS/Windows custom-prefix cases each returned `null` instead of `npm`; the pinned prefix-probe case also returned `null`; unmanaged status reported `npm` instead of `unknown`; admission lacked inspection diagnostics. All pass with the fix.
- Real isolated macOS npm proof: nvm-shaped Node 26.8.2 path, `~/.npm-global` launcher/package, `~/.npmrc` prefix line, no prefix environment variables. npm 11.19.1, shared update admission, and target selection all resolved the custom npm prefix.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` — passed on the final consolidated tree, including core/test typechecks, full core lint, dead-export scans, and zero runtime import cycles. `git diff --check` passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/tsgo-core-test-shards.test.ts -t 'covers the repository test roots exactly once with headroom below the hard cap'` — passed; the 700-root budget is unchanged.
- Initial CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34701614339 exposed an extra npm prefix probe on standalone packages. The repair checks global layout eligibility before probing; the existing runner test passes with its strict command-list assertion unchanged. The next run, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34702550786, caught the added test file exceeding the infra shard's 700-root budget. The cases now live in the existing npm lifecycle suite, preserving all assertions and the unchanged budget. Pre-fixup CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34703250632 completed successfully at `5ac8222475adf21334383ebac679cfb20da54177`. The exact-head watcher reports GREEN with zero pending checks after reconciling 12 superseded contexts.

Known gaps: the exact reason the reporter's npm probe differed is unconfirmed; stock npm correctly reads an isolated `~/.npmrc`. The regression models the observed mismatching probe and proves the missing launcher inference. No full Linux Testbox update/dry-run or published-driver-to-candidate update was run; platform layout tests and the isolated npm/admission proof cover this bounded repair. The installed 2026.9.3 updater cannot acquire this fix before admission; the reporter's explicit prefix environment workaround is still needed to get past that older driver.


Latest fixup CI: [run 34705209671](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34705209671) at `c2731dda081009379f6661654552872db16db6b4` is blocked by [checks-node-compact-small-29](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34705209671/job/103584079440): `test/scripts/tsgo-core-test-shards.test.ts:51` reports `gateway-other: 701 test roots exceeds the 700 limit`. This is inherited from main: the CI merge `6f7bfd32b498b4e4db228633376113c479ba2ac2` and its main parent `31c8b990cb5c95741796a3c79727cd0dc3e3be4a` have identical gateway tests, shard configs, and shard checker, with 701 matching gateway-other test paths in both. This PR adds no test files. That attempt stopped before the native wrapper; no budget or assertion was weakened. The main shard repair is now present in refreshed merge ref `1580397fd2ef54a4c2a73d30446031a50bb62df4` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 5587a15c3d1 refs/pull/146091/merge` passed). Fresh pull-request CI https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34707801181 passed on the unchanged approved head `c2731dda081009379f6661654552872db16db6b4`; the exact-head watcher reported GREEN with zero pending checks.

## ClawSweeper review

Maintainer decision: land this bounded ownership repair with the documented full published-driver upgrade qualification gap. Detection and target-selection evidence do not claim a complete upgrade transition. The lead re-reviewed and approved `c2731dda081009379f6661654552872db16db6b4` after the Windows fixup.

Applied the Windows npm shim finding: ownership detection now selects the package entrypoint immediately before `%*`, skipping npm's preceding `node.exe` existence check. The existing fixture now contains the complete npm-generated shim. With only that fixture changed, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-global-lifecycle.test.ts -t 'recognizes a custom npm prefix'` failed on Windows with `expected null to be 'npm'` (1 failed, 2 passed); with the parser fix, 143 tests passed across the lifecycle, global, Bun, pnpm discovery, status, and CLI command-runner suites. The bounded fixup passed Codex autoreview through P2 and `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/infra/update-global.ts src/infra/update-global-lifecycle.test.ts` (including core/test typechecks, lint, dead exports, and repository guards).

The data-model request is inapplicable: `update-check.ts` derives installation status and this diff adds no persistent schema, retention, or recovery changes. Full published-driver-to-candidate preservation proof remains an explicit limitation of this bounded landing, as recorded above; it is not claimed by the layout tests. Older installed updaters still need `NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX` for the first hop.
